A thunderstorm produced a tornado in Pecos County approximately 19 miles north northwest of Fort Stockton. This tornado was seen and reported by a spotter. This tornado was difficult to photograph as it quickly became rain-wrapped and eventually dissipated as the storm approached State Highway 18 in northern Pecos County. This tornado was estimated to have lasted around 12 minutes and traveled southeast approximately 4.5 miles. These calculations were determined from both radar data and eyewitness reports on the ground. Due to the rural location of this tornado, access to any damage indicators was impossible and thus the tornado was rated EF-Unknown with unknown peak wind speeds. The path width of the tornado is unknown.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado to the west of Highway 67 in Pecos County about 17 miles northeast of Fort Stockton. Given the proximity to the highway, many storm spotters were able to identify and photograph this tornado. Based upon eyewitness reports, videos, and radar data, this tornado tracked northeastward for two and a half miles and was estimated to have lasted around ten minutes. Due to the rural nature of this tornado and lack of access to damage indicators, this tornado was rated EF-Unknown with unknown peak wind speeds. The path width is also unknown.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado in Pecos County approximately seven miles to the east northeast of Fort Stockton and two miles north of I-10. This tornado only briefly touched down, lasting less than a minute, and no damage was reported. Given that no damage indicators were accessible, this tornado was rated an EF-Unknown with unknown peak wind speeds. The path width is also unknown.

A thunderstorm moved across Pecos County and produced wind damage one mile southeast of Fort Stockton. Damage to travel trailers was reported in Rooney Park and trees were uprooted. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage in Pecos County two miles east northeast of Fort Stockton. This damage was determined to be caused by rear-flank downdraft winds with estimated peak wind speeds of 90 mph. The damage included multiple destroyed billboards, two damaged metal buildings, and two 18-wheelers flipped along I-10. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado in Scurry County in and near the town of Hermleigh. The tornado touched down approximately one mile northwest of Hermleigh near the intersection of County Road 4111 and County Road 4116. The tornado snapped numerous power poles as it crossed over County Road 4111 and continued moving east northeast. As the tornado approached US Highway 84, it produced EF-2 level damage at a home and detached garage where most of the roofing material was ripped off and concrete anchorage failure occurred. Large vehicles, trailers, and other debris were scattered up to 100 yards west of this home. The tornado continued onward, crossing US Highway 84 where it impacted a trailer park. Numerous mobile homes were flipped or tossed towards the west southwest as the backside of the tornadic circulation passed over the RV park. The tornado continued moving northeast and eventually occluded on the north side of town. Peak wind speeds in the tornado were estimated to be approximately 115 mph. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Scurry County and produced wind damage. The areas of damage were northwest of Hermleigh, locations to the south of a tornado that impacted the northwest side of Hermleigh, and a rural area east of Dunn. This damage included snapped power poles, significant damage to trees and roofs, and an overturned manufactured home. Given the orientation of the damage, and re-analyzing the radar data, this damage was determined to be caused by rear-flank downdraft winds, with estimated peak wind speeds of 85-100 mph. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado near State Highway 158 in Glasscock County. This tornado crossed State Highway 158 and lasted about fifteen minutes before dissipating after crossing County Road 130. Power poles were snapped and completely blown over in the opposite direction along Highway 158. A narrow swath of power poles were snapped along County Road 110 and a lone power pole was snapped off County Road 130. Video evidence from Highway 158 shows this tornado was multi-vortex with three to four ground circulations evident. The tornado likely touched down multiple times along the path. The path length and location are estimated by radar and power pole damage locations. The path width is unknown. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

There was no apparent damage from the reported tornado in the location supplied by storm chasers and estimated by radar data. Video evidence from storm chasers shows the tornado lasted only 29 seconds before lifting in a rural area with limited damage indicators. No damage was found, this tornado has been rated EF-Unknown and the time and location of this tornado was estimated by radar data. Path length and width are also estimated.

A tornado began near the I-10 and Hwy 67 junction east of Fort Stockton in Pecos County. Damage indicators show that the tornado began as an EF-0 before growing in width and strengthening to an EF-1 about 5 minutes after it began. The tornado continued in a southeast direction as an EF-1 before dropping to an EF-0 just before lifting around 20 minutes after it began.

One eyewitness captured a tornado likely in the dissipating stage roughly 10 miles southwest of Sheffield. It is possible the tornado lasted shorter or longer than the estimated time and may have lifted and touched down at multiple points along the path. The survey team was unable to reach the path of the tornado and no damage indicators were found, thus this tornado is classified as an EF-Unknown. Path width is also estimated.

A few storm chasers reported a tornado northeast of Fort Stockton that lifted within a few minutes after they spotted it. Their videos and photos were used in conjunction with radar to determine the approximate path and time of this tornado. Due to the rural location and lack of damage indicators, no damage was found and the tornado was rated EF-Unknown. Path width is also estimated.

Due to the rural location and lack of damage indicators, no damage was found and the tornado was rated an EF-Unkown. Photos and radar were used to estimate path length and time. This tornado likely began as a weak, uncondensed tornado near Highway 80 and FM 1788, causing minor damage as it tracked towards I-20 and FM 1788. The tornado was then observed crossing I-20 and becoming a dusty circulation, causing damage to power poles, buildings, and RVs near CR1270. NWS employees could see this tornado from the office to the south of I-20. A strong RFD surge overtook the circulation after this time. Reports indicated the tornado may have dissipated, but it most likely became shrouded in rain and dust as a very intense couplet quickly developed as the circulation moved south-southwest. A VROT of 90-100 knots was observed on KMAF radar data at its peak. Limited damage indicators existed during its peak intensity. Minor damage was reported southeast after this time as the circulation slowly weakened and broadened, potentially becoming a larger, multivortex circulation. This tornado likely reached its peak width of approximately a mile wide at this time. This tornado likely dissipated a short time later to the southwest as the TDS dissipated. Property damage cost is an estimation.

NWS employees spotted a secondary, smaller, and weaker circulation to the east of the strengthening Warfield tornado. The NWS survey team was unable to find damage in the area, as this weak satellite tornado likely occurred over open terrain. This tornado was, therefore, rated EF-Unknown. The time and location of this brief tornado are estimated from radar data and reports.

This tornado was reported to have begun as a large tornado very near the Midland/Upton County line by multiple observers. This tornado began to move towards the west, growing in size and increasing in intensity as it caused EF-3 damage to vegetation and heavy oil equipment. Ground scouring was noted along this portion of the damage path. The tornado may have been nearly stationary for a short time before moving back to the west, continuing to cause damage to vegetation, power poles, and oil equipment. During this portion of the path, the tornado would cross from Midland County into Upton County, a short distance from FM 1788. Eventually, the tornado began to dissipate as it continued towards the west-southwest as a stringing cone tornado before ending. Property damage cost is an estimation.

Photos showed a tornado formed very near Sanderson along a ridge northwest of town. This tornado immediately entered a neighborhood west of US Highway 285 in Sanderson. Damage in this neighborhood included damage to walls and roofs of several houses with the complete destruction of a manufactured home. A sturdy steel carport collapsed in on itself, and trees were debarked in the area. This damage was rated with a max estimated wind speed of 140 MPH, making this tornado an EF-3. This tornado would continue a short distance to the east of this neighborhood, moving shipping containers and snapping power poles before lifting. Property damage cost is an estimation. Additionally, 12 injuries were reported, one was critical.

The same supercell thunderstorm that caused the first tornado would quickly produce another smaller tornado near the center of Sanderson a short time later. This tornado was photographed as a skinny rope tornado moving roughly parallel to Oak Street. This tornado would snap power poles, damage roofs, and destroy a small wooden building before lifting. This short-lived tornado was rated an EF-1 with peak winds estimated to have been 110 MPH. Property damage cost is an estimation.

Reports from the Texas Department of Transportation indicated that a substantial portion of State Route 170 was closed due to high water, southeast of Presidio, TX to near Lajitas, TX. In addition, the high water levels resulted in back flow up various tributaries to the Rio Grande River.  City officials reported flooding in the Loma Peloma and Redford areas.  Homes, 5 miles east of Presidio, were also threatened by the flood waters.||Low lying portions of Presidio, TX were under a mandatory evacuation for several days, which affected nearly 500 people.

Numerous roofs throughout Midland, TX were damaged during this event.  A local newspaper clipping with a quote from a major roofing company estimated 40 to 50 percent of the homes in Midland needed to be re-roofed.  The average cost to replace a shingled roof is anywhere from $8-$10K.  This resulted in an estimated $160 million in roof damage.  In addition to homes being damaged, multiple vehicles also received damage from the hail.  According to local dent repair shops and car dealers across the area, an estimated 800 vehicles had to be repaired resulting in $1.2 million in damage.  A Midland woman was also struck in the stomach by a hail stone, after it broke through her dining room window.  Her injuries were only minor and did not require medical attention.

Although a tornado was never reported during the time of issuance, later public reports and a NWS Storm Survey indicated in fact there was a tornado.  Based on radar estimates, tornadic damage began sometime around 4 PM CST about 28 miles north of Dryden, TX.  This is where a 30 gallon fiberglass tank was destroyed, in addition to another chemical tank.  Pieces of the fiberglass tank were found downwind.  A set of metal stairs that appeared to have been welded to the tank were also found downwind and were no longer attached to the tank.  As the tornado tracked southeastward, its debris field of rocks, gravel and tree limbs stripped the paint off of a recently painted 300 gallon storage tank.  The tornado continued on its path and weakened after stripping some cedar trees sometime around 404 PM CST.  Please see the attached images for damage photos and a detailed image of the tornado's damage path.
It is unknown whether or not a tornado actually developed.

This tornado first did damage to 7 power poles about 4.5 miles southwest of Tarzan; this was confirmed by contacting the utility company in the area the following day.  The estimated time of damage according to radar at this location was around 2020 CST.  At 2032 CST, the tornado then tracked east northeastward and impacted a COOP observer's farm about 3 miles southeast of Tarzan, TX damaging multiple pieces of farm equipment, storage tanks and removing 3 roofs from multiple structures.  It then continued on its same path snapping 3 power poles about a mile west of Lenorah, TX.  The estimated time of damage according to radar was sometime around 2036 CST.  This was the last known location of the tornado, although another tornado redeveloped with the same supercell about 20 minutes later.  Please see the attached images.

A large funnel cloud was reported by a trained spotter around 2045 CST about 5 miles SSE of Tarzan.  It is possible that the funnel was actually a tornado considering the damage to the power poles done upstream.

A damage survey conducted across west central Martin County concluded that there was a tornado that tracked northeastward for approximately 7 miles, doing minor damage on the way.  The first signs of damage were observed at a residence where a 10'X6'X6' wooden storage structure was blown to the east northeast about 60 feet.  According to radar imagery, this was near 2055 PM CST.  In addition, minor roof damage was done to the home by west winds and the family's trampoline was wrapped around a nearby tree in the backyard.  The tornado then continued northeastward where it passed just to the north of two power poles that were snapped at the ground by damaging west winds sometime around 2112 PM CST.  The closest estimate of the path taken by the tornado has been attached.

At 1953 CST, a trained weather spotter reported a tornado about 5 miles northwest of Big Spring.  The NWS Storm Survey confirmed two snapped power poles, minor tree damage and an empty oil pump storage tank knocked over near this location.  The tornado then tracked north northeastward and bent an 80 foot aluminum radio tower in half towards the east and snapped two additional power poles due to damaging northerly winds on its northwest flank; this occurred sometime around 2000 CST.  At 2005 CST, another trained spotter reported a tornado near the town of Fairview, TX.  The damage survey concluded this was a valid report, as the tornado began to turn right snapping multiple power poles and damaging a 12���X10��� storage shed anchored 2-3 feet in the ground along the way.  The storage shed was tossed east northeast approximately 30 yards, indicating the tornado passed north of the residence.  As the tornado continued eastward just north of Farm to Market Road 2230 east of Fairview, a significant line of power pole damage (2 miles) was observed.  There were a total of 28 poles snapped towards the south around 2015 CST.  Twenty of these were distribution poles and 8 of these were larger transmission poles.  The tornado then possibly weakened and turned left to the northeast.  On its way, it damaged another storage shed and a home's north side windows approximately 4 miles northeast of Fairview.  The last approximated time for tornadic wind damage was around 2030 CST.  The path recorded for this event is not the exact path the tornado actually took.  Please see attached image.

The time and location were adjusted for this event according to radar.  The original report time was after the storm had passed.

The National Park Dispatch Center reported flowing water over SH 120 just north of the Rio Grande Village.  Although multiple vehicles hydroplaned near this location, no accidents or injuries were reported.
The hail covered the road and was about 2 inches deep.

A NWS Storm Survey concluded that damage was done to 44 power poles near Ranch Road 2627 in Brewster County, TX.  Some of the poles were snapped 3 to 4 feet above the ground and all the poles fell to the south as the storm moved in the same direction around 20 mph.  The poles were not consecutively snapped in a row.  At times, there were 15 snapped...then a gap...and then more snapped as you moved southeastward down the line.  Please see the attached images for a detailed look at the damage path.
Several road closures were reported by the fire department in Fort Davis, TX.
The hail covered the ground about 4 inches in depth.

The local law enforcement reported roads were impassible at 1530 CST due to high water and a motorist was stranded at Nelson and 1st Street.  The motorist was not injured.  In addition, the public reported standing water depths of 1 foot and multiple softball fields covered with water in Fort Stockton at 1536 CST.
Damage was reported at the KOA campground, including damage to several motor homes. The hail was 2 to 3 inches deep.
Sixty to seventy mph wind gusts reduced the visibility to 15 feet in blowing dust.

Cotton and alfalfa crops were damaged near Atoka, NM.  The Quentin Rogers cotton fields were stripped down to bare ground, while a 3 foot tall hay field near East Blevins Road and Highway 385 was stripped down to 10 inches tall.
Several homes and vehicles received significant damage due to the large hail.

The most extensive damage during this event was confined to the eastern portions Jal, NM with the most notable damage along State Highway 128 in the vicinity of the Lea County/Jal Airport.  At this location, a small single engine plane was flipped over.   Also, numerous aircraft hanger doors were blown in due to the high winds which resulted in extensive damage to several aircraft storage buildings.  Along State Highway 128, 28 power poles stretched along the southern edge of the highway were blown over into the eastbound lane of traffic.  Overall, a total of 60 power poles were damaged.  Closer to the city, numerous residential structures received significant roof damage, mainly in the form of lost roof shingles.  Several trees were also downed near the Jal Lake Recreational Area.
The wind gusts were estimated to be near 50 to 60 mph by law enforcement.  No damage was reported.

The roof of a slightly modified mobile home was blown off by outflow winds well ahead of any significant convection.  Rain was observed 25 minutes after the winds.  The debris associated with the roof also caused some minor damage to adjacent homes.
Two distribution power poles were blown down due to damaging winds.  A 60 mph wind gust was also measured at the Lea County Coop Plant.

Damage was done to a 24 story building near downtown Midland, TX.  Large wood panels, each weighing between 200 to 300 pounds 4'x4'x1', were torn off the outside of the structure near the 6th and 7th floors.  This has required the building to be re-engineered, with the removal of an additional 150 panels from the structure.  The time of this report was estimated.
The damaging winds associated with this storm blew over a carport and broke large tree limbs up to 8 to 10 inches in diameter.
Mesa Vineyard lost eighty percent of their grapes due to hail damage.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust picked up a camper trailer.  No significant damage was reported.
There were no damage reports with this gust.
Although damage was not reported with this wind gust, blowing dust resulted in reduced visibilities.
Several large rocks up to the size of basketballs were removed from SH 118 due to the flash flooding across the highway.
A carport and small outbuilding were destroyed by thunderstorm wind gusts.
Law enforcement reported multiple county roads were barricaded near Malaga, NM due to high water.  Sandbags were also used to prevent flooding near homes.

The sheriff's office reported that they were barricading low water crossing near Otis due to 1 to 2 feet of flowing water through some intersections.  Sandbags were also used to prevent flooding near homes.  No damage was reported, however.
Law enforcement reported that the roads were impassible at the intersection of 42nd and Dixie due to high water.

There were numerous damage reports associated with this severe thunderstorm.  The damage path has been estimated according to these reports.  At 1945 MST, a trained spotter reported that a small camper was blown over onto a pickup truck near the intersection of Kincaid Rd and Highway 385.  Significant damage was done to the camper.  About five minutes later, 30' long by 20' wide metal sheds were destroyed about 5 miles south of Artesia and an Atoka, NM resident had his porch awning blown off his house.  Around 1955 MST, thunderstorm wind gusts snapped a power pole in half near the junction of 4 Dinkus Rd and Highway 285.
Eight inches of flowing water was observed near the intersection of Scarborough and A Street.
There was no significant damage reported with this estimated gust.

There were multiple reports of flash flooding, mainly across western Midland County.  Flash flooding was first reported on Loop 250 and the adjacent access roads between Tremont and Holiday Hill Roads at 1138 PM CST, where there was 6 inches of flowing water present.  The next location of flooding was reported at the intersection of Andrews Highway and Midland Drive at 1141 PM CST.  Cars were also stranded at the intersection of Andrews Highway and Idlewild Road at 1146 PM CST.  Finally, substantial flooding was reported by TEXDOT at 1152 PM CST and likely continued for another 30 minutes before the storm weakened.
Law enforcement reported multiple high water rescues do to flash flooding near the intersections of 2nd Street and West County Road, and Wendover and Penbooke Roads at 1148 CST.
Several 16 foot by 3 inch diameter tree branches were snapped off pecan trees.

In addition to the measured wind gust at the mesonet, a trampoline was blown through a residence's roof.  The time of occurrence was not available, but it can be assumed that it happened near the same time of the wind observation.

There were numerous reports of flooding from multiple sources, but most were confirmed by the media.  At 515 AM CST, the Midland Police Department reported a few stalled vehicles across the city limits.  Three minutes later, a high water rescue was reported at the intersection of Lee and Maple.  At 635 AM CST, the media reported flash flooding along the Scharbauer Draw in residential areas.  The police department then reported two more cars were submerged in the city of Midland, at 717 AM CST.  One foot of flowing water was present near the intersection of Golf Course and Garfield.  Finally, at 1001 AM CST, the media still continued to report areas of high water across Midland.

The first flash flood report received for this event was from the Odessa Police Department.  At 710 AM CST, several roads were covered in water throughout the city limits.  The media reported the water depth was estimated to be 15 to 20 inches deep near the intersection of 36th and Dixie.  Finally, at 901 AM CST, another media crew reported many areas across Odessa were flooded with high water.
The top of a gazebo was blown off at a local residence.
Three power poles were knocked down by severe wind gusts.  In addition, 6-8 inch diameter tree limbs were snapped.
Some roads were impassable due to high water.  The duration of this event was estimated due to limited reports.
There were several impassible points along the Ross Maxwell Scenic Road due to high water.
A vehicle was reported submerged within the city limits in Andrews.  Roads on the northwest and northeast side of the city also had 1 foot of flowing water over them.
Multiple vehicles were submerged at the intersection of 23rd Street and Andrews Highway in Odessa.  In addition, 12 to 16 inches of flowing water covered the same roadway.
One intersection in Jal, NM had 2 to 3 feet of flowing water over the roadway.
The post office in Loco Hills, NM estimated winds to be near 70 mph or greater, although no damage was officially reported.
A trained spotter reported numerous tree limbs, up to 4 inches in diamter, were blow down in Artesia, NM.
The spotter's car windshield was broken and the hail also dented the vehicle.
Multiple power poles were knocked down in Carlsbad, NM.
A roof was blown off of a home approximately 15 miles south of Carlsbad, NM.
A powper pole was reported knocked down near the Winkler/Loving county line.
Local law enforcement reported water up to the windows of a vehicle at a well known low water crossing.
No damage was reported.
Law enforcement reported a roof was blown off an old small structure and trees were downed by thunderstorm winds.
No damage was reported with this event.
Local law enforcement reported multiple power lines were downed due the strong winds.  The number of power poles/lines damaged was not available.
A total of 7 distribution power poles were knocked down/snapped along County Road 101 just south of Wink, TX.
One distribution power pole was knocked down near the intersection of County Road 202 and State Highway 302.
Flash flooding was reported at the intersection of FM 1788 and Business 20.  A few vehicles were stalled in the high water.
Downed power poles were reported on the northeast side of Odessa.  The number of power poles was not reported, and therefore, the monetary damage was estimated for this event.
No damage was reported with this event.
One to two inch diameter tree limbs were snapped by the winds.
A transmission power pole was reported down along State Highway 118.
Due to heavy rain, Terlingua Creek rapidly filled in the Big Bend National Park.  Water up to 2 1/2 feet in depth covered roadways in the park.  The roads were barricaded by park officials.
A power pole was knocked down between the cities of Tatum and Lovington, NM.  The exact location of the report was not available.  Therefore, the location was estimated according to radar.

A Texas Tech Mesonet extension agent reported tennis ball size hail and extensive hail damage to sorghum and cotton crops near the area.  Public reports indicated over 4500 acres of cotton were destroyed by the hail.  In addition, 1000 acres of sorghum were destroyed.  Several homes also sustained roof damage from the large hail.

Damaging winds, estimated to be near 80 mph and measured at 73 mph by a local resident, first snapped power poles near State Highway 137 over extreme northwestern Reagan County Texas around 1740 CST.   As the storm progressed north northeastward, a residence along State Highway 137 (just south of the county line) also sustained damage to its property near 1745 CST.  Numerous tree branches, some 8 to 12 inches in diameter, were snapped.  Two windows on the southwest corner of the home were also broken by the strong winds, and a windmill near the back of the home was bent in half.  From 1810 to 1820 CST, the storm continued north northeastward and snapped/downed multiple power poles. The most significant damage caused by the storm was at a residence along Farm Road 2401 about 1 mile east of the SH137/FM2401 intersection.  Here, large pine tree branches about one foot in diameter were snapped near the top of the tree.  A large A-frame metal barn was also heavy damaged, with both doors bent from a south to north direction.  The winds funneled through this structure and pushed a 4 ton trailer about 60 feet outside of the building.  This was near the end of the damage path around 1820 CST. Overall, 60 or more power poles were damaged during this event.

Rio Grande Electric Coop and the public reported wind damage from Lajitas, TX to Terlingua, TX.  The severe winds first damaged the roof of a home and 6 power poles in Lajitas around 1700 CST.  As the storm moved northeastward, it snapped 4 more power poles along State Highway 170 from Lajitas to Terlingua.
Rio Grande Electric Coop reported 2 power poles were downed near Panther Junction, TX.  The severe winds also damaged a roof to a hotel/lodge near the same area.
The high winds did damage to a portion of a newly placed frame for a library in Alpine, TX.  A monetary estimate for the damage was made according to a picture provided by a local news affiliate.
Sustained winds of at least 40 mph were observed at the Pine Springs ASOS for several hours, with a maximum gust of 64 mph observed at 2019 MST.
The winds were likely higher, but the equipment failed after the wind gusted to 86 MPH.

events.event_narrative: Roof decking was ripped off a building, along with windows being blown out of the same structure in Pine Springs.  In addition, several wind turbines in the Delaware Mountains were also destroyed by the high winds.  A monetary damage estimate for the wind turbines is not currently available.
A gust of 78 MPH was measured with a hand held anemometer by the observer.
Semi trucks were blown over along U.S. Highway 62/180 just near Pine Springs.  A monetary damage estimate was not available for this report.
Two power poles were blown down/snapped in Carlsbad, NM.  In addition, a carport was ripped from its foundation and blown 200 feet.
Six power poles were blown down/snapped in Eunice and Jal.
A pressure tank weighing 160 pounds on a water well was blown over and sparked a wildfire 5 miles southeast of Andrews.
A roof was blown off a private residence 2 miles east of Andrews.
A tree measuring 6 feet in diameter was blown into a utility pole, which destroyed the transformer and snapped the pole.
Several PVC tent poles were snapped.
Fifteen power poles were blown down/snapped in Hobbs, NM.
A metal roof was peeled off a mobile home and a warehouse in Hobbs.
This wind gust was measured by hand held anemometer.
A DPS trooper used a hand held anemometer to measure the 112 MPH gust at the base of Guadalupe Pass.
A 70 MPH gust was measured at the McDonald Observatory.  Heavy snow was occurring when a 70 MPH gust was recorded at McDonald Observatory at 1830 LST.
Several gusts of 60 MPH or greater were recorded at the Mount Locke Observatory.
Freezing rain, sleet and freezing fog resulted in 0.01-0.02 inches of ice accumulation mainly on elevated objects, 7 miles WNW of Alpine.
Two inches of snow accumulated at Queen on 11/30/09, but the two day total was 13 inches of snowfall.
Four to eight inches of snow accumulated in and near Carlsbad from 11/30/09 to 12/01/09.
Two to four inches of snow fell in and near Tatum from 11/30/09 to 12/01/09 in northern Lea county.
Four inches of snow accumulated in and near Fort Davis from 11/30/09 to 12/01/09.
Eight inches of snow accumulated at the Mcdonald Observatory from 11/30/09 to 12/01/09.  The Observatory is located 9 miles northwest of Fort Davis.
Two inches of snow accumulated in and near Marfa from 11/30/09 to 12/01/09.
Two inches of snow fell in and near Tatum from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
Three inches of snow fell in Hope from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
Three inches of snow fell in Hope from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
Three inches of snow fell in Carlsbad from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
One to one and a half inches fell in Hobbs from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
One half to one inch of snow fell in Jal from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
Two inches of snow fell in Queen from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
Three to four inches of snow fell in Van Horn from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.

events.event_narrative: Two inches of snow fell in Pecos on 12/04/09.
One to one and a half inches of snow fell in Kent on 12/04/09.
One half to one inch of snow fell in Alpine on 12/04/09.
One inch of snow fell in Sanderson on 12/04/09.
One inch of snow fell in Seminole from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
One ot one and a half inches of snow fell in Kermit from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.

One inch of snow fell in Odessa on 12/04/09.  The Odessa Division of the Texas Department of Transportation reported traffic accidents on Interstate 20 on the southeast side of Odessa.  Traffic diverted to the service road until the accidents were cleared.

One inch of snow fell at the Midland International Airport from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.|The Odessa Division of the Texas Department of Transportation reported a tractor trailer rollover in the median on Interstate 20 on the southwest side of Midland due to an icy road.  The truck was leaking fuel.  Traffic was redirected to the service road until the accident was cleared.
One inch of snow fell in Fort Stockton on 12/04/09.
One half to one and a half inches of snow fell in Big Spring on 12/04/09.
One inch of snow fell in Bakersfield on 12/04/09.
Three inches of snow fell in McCamey on 12/04/09.
One inch of snow fell in Garden City on 12/04/09.
One inch of snow fell in Stanton from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
One inch of snow fell in Lamesa from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.

Two inches of snow fell in Andrews from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.  The Odessa Division of the Texas Department of Transportation reported a single car rollover near Andrews on the night of 12/03/09.  Driver and passengers taken to the hospital for a variety of injuries.

events.cz_name: REEVES COUNTY AND UPPER TRANS PECOS
events.event_narrative: Three to five inches of snow fell in Balmorhea on 12/04/09.
Two inches of snow fell 12 miles west of Fort Davis on 12/04/09.
Four to five inches of snow fell at Guadalupe Mountains National Park from 12/03/09 to 12/04/09.
One to one and a half inches of snow fell 8 miles south of Kent on 12/04/09.
Three inches of snow fell in Big Lake on 12/04/09.
One inch of snow fell 26 miles east-southeast of Fort Stockton on 12/04/09.

The Texas Department of Transportation reported numerous accidents, jack-knifed tractor trailers and vehicles sliding off roadways across the region due to snow packed and icy roads at 0950 LST 12/04/09.  The intersection of Interstate Highway 10 with Interstate 20 about 40 miles west of Pecos had 6 inches of snow by this time too.

The El Paso and Odessa Divisions of the Texas Department of Transportation reported|Interstate Highway 10 closed from the merger of Interstate Highway 10 and Interstate Highway 20, 40 miles west of Pecos, to Mile Marker 170 or 6 miles west of Kent due to jack-knifed tractor trailer trucks on the icy highways.  Eastbound Interstate 10 traffic was stopped at Van Horn and westbound traffic was stopped at Fort Stockton or Balmorhea for most of the morning.  Westbound Interstate Highway 20 traffic was stopped at Pecos.
The Midland Emergency manager reported the closure of Loop 250 in Midland due to icy roads and the occurrence of several accidents at 2140 LST 12/07/09.
Strong winds blew the roofs off two mobile homes in Odessa.
Strong wind gust measured by a retired National Weather Service employee.
Strong wind gusts of 64 MPH were recorded around Noon LST at Tatum and Lovington.

Four to six inches of snow accumulated at McDonald Observatory in the Davis Mountains during the afternoon and evening of the 23rd.  Snowfall was heavy for two to three hours from 1800 to 2000 LST.  Highway 118 in Jeff Davis County near McDonald Observatory was snow packed and icy by 2000 LST.   Strong winds of 70 MPH were measured at McDonald Observatory at 1830 LST during the heavy snowfall.

Four inches of snow accumulated 22 miles northwest of Gail from the night of 12/23/09 until morning on 12/24/09.   North winds of 20 to 30 MPH and gusts near 50 MPH resulted in considerable blowing snow and snow drifts of 1 to 2 feet.
Four inches of snow was reported 4 miles south of Fluvanna.  Considerable blowing and drifting of snow occurred due to north winds of 20 to 30 MPH and gusts near 40 MPH on the morning of the 24th.

Four inches of snow was reported from Gail to Fluvanna on the morning of 12/24/09.  Rain that occurred prior to the precipitation turning to snow resulted in a thin layer of ice on U.S. Highway 180 between Gail and Fluvanna which was then covered by 3 to 4 inches of snow overnight.  North winds of 20 to 30 MPH and gusts near 50 MPH resulted in considerable blowing snow and snow drifts of 1 to 2 feet deep.

Six inches of snow accumlated in Inadale, or 18 miles southeast of Snyder.  North winds of 20 to 30 MPH and gusts near 50 MPH resulted in near white out conditions from blowing snow and snow drifts 2 feet deep on the morning of 12/24/09.

Five inches of snow accumulated in Loraine, or 8 miles east of Colorado City, on 12/24/09.  North winds of 20 to 30 MPH and gusts near 50 MPH resulted in near whiteout conditions and snow drifts 1 to 2 feet during the morning of 12/24/09.  The Mitchell County Sheriffs Office reported a tractor trailer was blown over on Interstate 20 at 0718 LST, 7 miles east of Colorado City.  They also reported a travel trailer was blown over on Interstate 20 at 0827 LST, 8 miles east of Colorado City.
Five and one half inches of snow accumulated in Carlsbad by 1115 LST.  Moderate to heavy snowfall in a 2 to 3 hour span resulted in 4 inches of snow accumulation in Carlsbad.
Four inches of snow accumulated in Tatum.  Roads were snow packed and icy.
Five inches of snow accumulated in Queen, most of which occurred between 0700 and 0900 LST with a burst of moderate to heavy snowfall.
Four inches of snow accumulated 2 miles north of Artesia.
Although there were only a few wind gusts, two occurrences of 59 MPH around 150 LST and another of 56 MPH at 251 LST.
There was also one gust of 59 MPH at 0000 LST 1/7/10.
Westerly winds peaked in the higher elevations of the Davis Mountains at 1220 LST with a 65 MPH measured gust at Mount Locke Observatory.
The stronger winds were more isolated on 1/22/10 and 1/23/10.  A peak wind gust of 64 MPH occurred twice, the first at 0800 1/21/10 and the second at 1200 LST on 1/22/10.

Strong westerly winds raked the lower elevations of the Guadalupe Mountains from 0551 LST on 1/21/10 to 1651 LST on 1/24/10 mainly in the morning and afternoon.  The stronger gusts of 92 MPH at 1128 LST and 90 MPH at 1051 LST on 1/22/10 were likely exacerbated by evaporational cooling of the column of air due to a dry subcloud layer and virga showers that occurred.  Sustained westerly winds of 56, 72, 55, and 60 MPH occurred at 0951, 1051, 1128 and 1151 LST respectively.
Sustained west winds of 40 MPH or greater occurred at Carlsbad from 0953 LST to 1353 LST on 1/23/10.
A sustained northwest wind of 46 MPH and gust of 59 MPH occurred at Artesia.  Virga showers and a dry subcloud layer likely enhanced the wind speeds.
Strong west winds occurred at Mount Locke Observatory.  Sustained winds of 40 to 45 MPH were accompanied by frequent gusts over 60 MPH and two gusts over 70 MPH on the afternoon of 1/22/10.

An 81 MPH gust occurred at 0345 LST 1/24/10 at McDonald Observatory in the Davis Mountains.  An extended high wind event occurred in the Davis Mountains with sustained winds above 40 MPH, and as high as 53 MPH, for an 18 hour period.  In addition, gusts exceeded 70 MPH frequently during this time.
No damage was observed with this report.
The skirting was ripped off a mobile home in Artesia due to the strong winds.
A mix of rain and sleet changed to snow over the Guadalupe Mountains on 1/23/10.  Queen received 7 inches of snow by 2200 LST on 1/23/10.
Four inches of snow accumulated at Queen in the foothills of the Guadalupe mountains in southwestern Eddy County.
Four inches of snow was reported by a trained spotter in Lamesa.
Five inches of snow was reported in Snyder.
A high water rescue was reported by the broadcast media near the intersection of FM1936 and I-20.
Local law enforcement reported cars were stalled at the intersection of 42nd and Dixie in Odessa, TX.  The water was up to car door handles.
Local law enforcement reported high water at the intersection of Andrews Highway and Illinois St.  Large construction barrels were seen floating down the road.
The public reported a barn was destroyed, a trampoline was blown into another yard, and several utility poles were snapped due to wind gusts associated with the storm.
A wind turbine was destroyed by the severe gust.  In addition, a cedar tree was also snapped near its base.
Guadalupe Mountains National Park Headquarters reported of 4 inches of snow.
Several reports of 3 to 5 inches of snow occurred across Mitchell County.

There were several reports across Midland County of 4 to 7 inches of snow.  Five  inches of snow was measured at the Weather Forecast Office in Midland.  Five  inches of snow was reported on the north side of Midland.
Four inches of snow was reported in Crane County.
Seven to eight inches of snow was reported in Big Spring.
Four inches of snow was reported in Rankin.
